mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction triggers a term premium compression, lowering discount rates and thereby increasing the present value of expected equity cash flows, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day rolling mean during the same month, or term premium expansion (measured via 10Y Treasury yield minus 3M TIPS) is observed instead.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below the prior 12-month average indicate deflationary pressure, which lowers real discount rates and increases the present value of equities, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls for three consecutive months below its 12-month lagged average
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in at least 70% of similar deflationary episodes, or real GDP growth exceeds 2% in the subsequent quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in unemployment (implied by UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 10% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by at least 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically significant (p > 0.10) relative to the prior 10-day mean during analogous labor market tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average, coupled with elevated retail sales momentum (implied by HOUST), indicates accelerating economic demand, which elevates earnings expectations and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above its 12-month moving average while HOUST increases by at least 5% month-over-month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns remain negative in 60% of analogous episodes with similar demand indicators turning positive.

mechanism_narrative: A multi-month decline in inventory levels (implied by INDPRO trending lower) suggests supply-side constraints, which can lead to temporary price supports and higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for three consecutive months below its 12-month low
regime_hint: Supply shock or inventory drawdown regime
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 90-day historical average during comparable supply shocks (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in payroll growth suggests a weakening labor market, which can trigger a risk-off spiral and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 15% month-over-month while PAYEMS_yrly_growth falls
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns remain positive or flat in 80% of prior labor market weakening episodes with similar signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for two consecutive months in the absence of a corresponding rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates a strong labor market and policy accommodation, which can compress real rates and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months while CPIAUCSL remains below 3.0% for the same period
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not higher than the 30-day historical average during analogous low-inflation, low-unemployment regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in retail activity (HOUST) while industrial production remains flat or rising indicates a sector-specific demand shock that can depress consumer sentiment and corporate earnings expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by at least 8% month-over-month while INDPRO does not increase by more than 2% over the same period
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically significant (p > 0.10) during analogous demand dislocation episodes.
